metadata.note: Yes -- Canandaigua, NY had passenger rail, and in fact was a significant railroad hub: the first train reached it September 12, 1840 via the Rochester and Auburn Railroad (not yet separately traced on this map -- see auburn_and_syracuse_railroad.geojson, whose own note flags this Rochester-Canandaigua-Auburn stretch as missing), and at its peak 36 passenger trains a day used the 1890 depot funded by Mrs. Thompson and the Vanderbilts. This file covers the Rochester and Eastern Rapid Railway (R&E), an electric interurban chartered 1901 that connected Rochester to Canandaigua (1903) and Geneva (1904) via the Pittsford-Fishers-Victor corridor, running down Main Street through Canandaigua itself. The New York Central took control via its Mohawk Valley Company subsidiary in 1905, folding the R&E into New York State Railways in 1909; service ended July 31 1930. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap for the Rochester-Pittsford, Bushnell's Basin-Fishers-Victor, and Seneca Castle-Geneva stretches; the Pittsford-Bushnell's Basin and Victor-Canandaigua-Seneca Castle stretches are straight-line approximations -- much of this route ran on streets (Rochester's Monroe Avenue, Canandaigua's Main Street) that carry no trace of the interurban today, and the implausible-detour check rejected the real-track paths OSM offered for these stretches as unrealistic loops through the wider regional rail network rather than the actual street-running alignment.

segments.note: The Rochester and Eastern Rapid Railway, chartered 1901 by Rochester investors, began service between Rochester and Canandaigua in 1903 (power house and car barn in Canandaigua), extending to Geneva by 1904. Departed Rochester on Monroe Avenue using Rochester Railway Company streetcar tracks; stops included Pittsford, Bushnell's Basin, Fishers, Victor, Mertensia, and Paddleford before Canandaigua, where the line ran down Main Street, then Hopewell, Seneca Castle, Gates, and Pre-emption to Geneva (terminating near City Hall on Castle Street). Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Consolidated in 1909 with other Rochester/Mohawk Valley area electric railways to form New York State Railways, wholly owned by the New York Central. Early success from Finger Lakes leisure travel gave way to automobile competition through the 1920s; a 1928 reroute connected to the Rochester Subway at Rowlands (see rochester_subway.geojson) for faster downtown service, but ridership kept falling. Legal permission to end all service was granted July 31 1930, followed by rapid dismantling. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
